claim: Intrinsic self-correction by a prompted LLM (no oracle, test or tool) does not reliably help and often lowers accuracy. Reported gains came from oracle stop labels, weak first prompts or unequal compute. Reasoning models still flip 8-16% of correct yes/no answers (o1-preview 13.2%, o1-mini 15.6%, R1 7.9%); a naive revision model turned about 38% of correct MATH answers wrong.
agent_test: Answer -> self-review -> revise with no tool signal vs single answer vs resample, equal tokens; count right-to-wrong and wrong-to-right flips.
audit_note: The 38% revision flip is PaLM 2-S* on MATH with a trained revision model (Snell et al.), and the 8-16% flips are on one Yes/No task; wording is slightly wide but numbers match.

claim: Reliable external feedback (sound verifier, test run, tool, human) is what makes revision pay; the model judging itself adds little. Blocksworld 40% alone, 55% with LLM verifier, 88% with sound validator; graph colouring 16% -> about 40% with sound verifier but 1/100 with GPT-4 self-critique; CRITIC without the tool falls back to near CoT; code repair 33.3% -> 52.6% with human feedback.
agent_test: Gate every revision on a code-run, test or checker result; compare with LLM-judge gating at equal tokens.

claim: Detection and localisation of the error is the bottleneck; fixing it once located is easy. Best model finds the first wrong step in only 52.87% (GPT-4, BIG-Bench Mistake); with the true location, backtracking gains +18 to +44 points on wrong traces. Failure attribution in multi-agent logs is 53.5% for the agent but 14.2% for the step. Gap search: Tyen's break-even is about 60-70% locator accuracy on BIG-Bench Mistake only; MR-GSM8K gives GPT-4-Turbo first-error-step accuracy 48.8.
agent_test: Compare code-located error line vs model-located vs none at equal tokens; measure fix rate given location.
audit_note: 'Fixing it is easy' is slightly generous: even with the true location, backtracking cost up to 11 points on originally correct traces.

claim: A false or invented error report does damage because models obey critique. They change 94% of edges named as wrong even when the report is false; correct traces lose 0 to 11 points under true-location backtracking and 7-16 points under random location; step-by-step CoT checking invents mistakes in correct traces. Any revise trigger needs high precision and a keep-best-so-far rule.
agent_test: Inject false error reports into a revise step and measure harm; test keep-best-so-far against always-accept-revision.
audit_note: The 94% obedience is for GPT-4 on graph colouring only.

claim: Models fix an error shown as someone else's but not the same error shown as their own (self-correction blind spot): 64.5% average over 14 open non-reasoning models; appending Wait cuts it by 89.3% and fine-tuning on 5,306 traces by 76.0%. Reasoning models show a small or negative blind spot. Gap search: the v2 text tests no Claude and no o1; the earlier Claude blind-spot figures were not re-found and are unverified. Wait on a non-reasoning base recovers most of the gap to the reasoning version (DeepSeek-V3 0.578 to 0.918 vs R1 0.908).
agent_test: Present the earlier answer as a colleague's draft and/or add a Wait cue at the review step vs same-voice review; equal tokens, same error set.

claim: Appending Wait to force more thinking helps a little on hard sets and then flattens (s1-32B AIME24 50.0 -> 53.3 at 2x, 57 at larger extrapolation; MATH500 flat at 93.0). Gap search: with repeated Wait, small distilled models flatten then fall (GSM8K 87.3% to 70.3% at 15,980 tokens); Claude models also lose accuracy on some tasks with longer reasoning (inverse scaling).
agent_test: Wait cue before stopping vs none at equal total tokens; check flat-after-one-use.
audit_note: The 87.3 to 70.3 figure is for a 1.5B distilled model (R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) on GSM8K.

claim: Reasoning-trained models locate the first wrong step better than most non-reasoning critics and small trained process reward models on ProcessBench (F1 o1-mini 87.9, QwQ-32B-Preview 71.5, GPT-4o 61.9, Llama-3.3-70B 58.0; Math-Shepherd-PRM-7B 47.9/29.5/24.8 on GSM8K/MATH/OlympiadBench), but they still flip correct answers when told to revise (DeepSeek R1 7.9% on a yes/no task).
agent_test: Re-test the code-locates, model-fixes split when the agent's base model is a reasoning model.
audit_note: 47.9/29.5/24.8 are one PRM (Math-Shepherd-PRM-7B on GSM8K/MATH/OlympiadBench), not open PRMs generally; Skywork-PRM-7B scores 70.8 on GSM8K, and the PRM average (e.g. 42.1 Skywork, 56.5 PRM800K PRM) is closer to non-reasoning critics.
claim_before_audit: Reasoning-trained models are much better at locating the first wrong step than non-reasoning critics or small trained process reward models: ProcessBench F1 o1-mini 87.9, QwQ-32B 71.5, GPT-4o 61.9, Llama-3.3-70B 58.0; open PRMs 47.9/29.5/24.8 on three subsets. But they still flip correct answers when told to revise (R1 7.9%).

claim: At equal number of responses, critique and debate rounds do not beat sampling plus majority vote: GSM8K self-consistency 82.5/85.3/88.2 (3/6/9 responses) vs debate 83.2/83.0; resampling at n=15 matched critique loops in graph colouring; code repair at equal budget 1.05x and 0.97x pass@k. Gap search: Self-Debugging with unit-test feedback beat extra sampling by sample count on code, token cost not controlled; voting plateaus near 100 samples (Large Language Monkeys).
agent_test: Spend the same tokens on N samples with vote vs one draft plus critique rounds; report both.
audit_note: Debate comparison is GPT-3.5 on GSM8K only; graph-colouring resampling result is GPT-4 on 100 instances.

claim: LLM judges and critics are high-precision, low-recall and share errors with the generator, so a model saying it looks fine is not evidence: ReaLMistake recall low for strong models; Self-Refine feedback said everything looks good in 94% of math cases; models from different companies agree on 0.60 of joint errors (HELM, chance 1/3); judges more entangled with the generator over-endorse wrong answers (rho 0.44-0.52). Blocksworld LLM verifier accepted 38 of 45 invalid plans (corrected, see critique). Gap search: self-preference is linked to self-recognition (abstract only); no Claude false-pass number found.
agent_test: Measure how often a same-family reviewer approves known-wrong drafts; compare with a cross-family or code reviewer.
audit_note: The 0.60 HELM agreement is for model pairs in general, not specifically different-company pairs; the ambiguous '(corrected, see critique)' remark is fine since Valmeekam's text (38 false positives; 54+7=61 correct) supports 38 of 45 invalid plans accepted, though its Table 2 headers are misaligned.

claim: Critique wording and format shift detection sharply: recall changes 16.9 +/- 20.3 points between two prompt wordings; Vicuna-13b flagged 22.04% as wrong with direct critique vs 4.8% with CoT (true error 51.63%); biased prompts drop GPT-4 CSQA to 66-73 while neutral prompts give 84.6 at temperature 0.
agent_test: Fix one neutral review wording; test two alternative wordings on the same drafts and report variance.
audit_note: Kamoi's 16.9 +/- 20.3 is reported as percent higher recall between two prompt types (Type 1 vs Type 2), averaged over 12 LLMs and 3 tasks.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction under fair settings (temperature 0, neutral prompt) may be neutral to slightly positive, a partial rebuttal of Huang et al.; gains are mostly inside noise on single datasets.
agent_test: Rerun Huang-style intrinsic loop with temperature 0 and neutral wording on our tasks.

claim: Training (multi-turn RL, SCoRe) gives the first significantly positive intrinsic self-correction on MATH (60.0 -> 64.4, +4.4; correct-to-incorrect flips 15.8% -> 1.4%), whereas prompting and offline SFT variants give negative or small deltas (base -11.2; Self-Refine -1.0; STaR base-data -14.2, STaR+ +0.4; Pair-SFT +1.8). Needs weights, so not a scaffold.
agent_test: Not testable without training; use as a ceiling reference.
audit_note: Numbers match Kumar et al. Table 1/2, but plain SFT is not uniformly non-positive: Pair-SFT gave +1.8 (small, vs SCoRe +4.4 called the first significantly positive delta); STaR+ +0.4.
claim_before_audit: Training (multi-turn RL, SCoRe) can create positive intrinsic self-correction (MATH 60.0 -> 64.4; right-to-wrong flips 15.8% -> 1.4%), but prompting and plain SFT cannot (base -11.2; STaR base-data variant -14.2, STaR+ variant +0.4). Needs weights, so not a scaffold.

claim: Humans catch slips (execution errors) themselves, mostly through mismatch between intention and the executed action, while diagnosis errors (mistakes) usually need an outside view (Woods; Sellen). Per a review (Blavier et al. 2005) quoting Doireau et al. 1997: self-detected errors are recovered in about 90% of cases, while detection by a third person is infrequent (about 30%); outsiders detect better if they are domain experts, if the error is a mistake, and if detection is close in time to the error.
agent_test: Test same-agent review vs fresh-context reviewer (no memory of the draft) on slip-type vs mistake-type seeded errors.
audit_note: Blavier et al. quote Doireau: self-detected errors are recovered in ~90% of cases, but ~30% is the rate of error detection by a third person (not recovery), so the two are not a like-for-like comparison; the review also notes Doireau's own experiments found the opposite (observers detected mistakes more easily than slips); slips are caught mostly via intention-vs-action mismatch (Sellen action-based), not plan-vs-outcome.
claim_before_audit: Humans catch slips (execution errors) themselves, mostly via mismatch between plan and outcome, but diagnosis errors (mistakes) need an outside view: self-detected errors recovered in about 90% of cases vs about 30% when detected by a third person (Doireau, quoted by a review); outsiders do better if expert and early.

claim: Human error detection fits evidence that keeps accumulating after the response; detection and correction are separable (antisaccade: all errors corrected, only half detected); in a paper-check task people missed 54.28% of planted errors with 1.84% false alarms.
agent_test: Add a post-answer second look that gathers new evidence (re-derive, run code) rather than re-reading; compare.

claim: Telling humans to slow down or training them on forcing strategies did not raise diagnostic accuracy (Norman 2014: 44.5% vs 45.0%, n=204; Sherbino 2014: 54% vs 48%, p=0.13), while reflection and consider-the-opposite show gains in other trials. Evidence is mixed.
agent_test: Compare a generic slow-down prompt against a specific consider-the-opposite step at equal tokens.

claim: Checklists: before-after studies show big drops (Haynes: death 1.5% -> 0.8%, complications 11.0% -> 7.0%; Pronovost ICU infections IRR 0.34 at 16-18 months), but the population-level Ontario study found none (mortality 0.71% -> 0.65%, OR 0.91, P=0.13; complications 3.86% -> 3.82%).
agent_test: Test a short check list run by code against none, and measure whether benefit survives across task types.

claim: Errors are routine in expert systems and are best managed by layered defences and detection, not eliminated: LOSA over 3,500 flights found two threats and two errors per flight, more than half of errors violations; Reason: about 90% of maintenance quality lapses blameless. But the Swiss cheese model is read inconsistently (66.5% match, 30.6% place active error as hole) and has no measured effect size for agents.
agent_test: Count how many seeded faults pass 1, 2, 3 independent checks (code, fresh reviewer, same-model self-review) and check layer independence.
audit_note: Perneger 30.6% is the share who correctly placed active error as a hole; 'no measured effect size for agents' is an absence claim not checked exhaustively.

claim: Layers only help if their failures are independent; LLM layers from related models are not (correlated error 0.60 on HELM, 0.423 on HF vs chance 1/3 and 0.12), so stacking same-family reviewers gives less than Swiss-cheese arithmetic predicts. Gap search: Weaver gets up to +8.5% from 15 verifiers with diminishing gains and an independence assumption; same-family joint miss rate still unmeasured.
agent_test: Measure joint miss rate of two reviewers vs product of single miss rates.
audit_note: Minor: HF chance baseline is ~0.127 (rounded to 0.12); Weaver does report verifier score correlations (Table 16), only same-family joint miss rates are unmeasured; 'less than Swiss-cheese arithmetic predicts' is an inference.

claim: Multi-agent systems fail often (41% to 86.7% across 7 frameworks) and verification failures (premature termination, no or incomplete verification, incorrect verification) are about one fifth of failure modes (21.3% group share; 6.2%, 8.2%, 9.1% for the three modes). Prompt-level role fixes gave only +9.4% on ChatDev.
agent_test: Check which MAST verification modes our agent shows in its own traces.

claim: Spontaneous mid-reasoning self-correction and aha moments are weak or negative markers of a right answer (shift in 6.31% of traces; Qwen2.5-1.5B 2.57% correct with shift vs 16.44% without), yet forced reconsideration helps where entropy is high; reasoning models often keep a planted error in the chain and still answer right (55-78%).
agent_test: Compare self-initiated backtracking vs forced Wait at a chosen point; do not use backtracking count as a quality signal without validation.

claim: Label-free agreement signals between samples are a usable cheap error flag and routing rule: disagreement-guided routing raised the 7-benchmark math average 61.3 -> 75.8 (Qwen3-8B, cap 6 samples); risk-controlled abstention kept selective risk below 1.5% at 76.1% coverage; self-consistency N=5 gave AUROC 0.823 for wrong-answer prediction. Gap search: semantic-entropy style agreement flags uncertainty but is untested on shared-wrong-belief cases; vote plateaus.
agent_test: Use sample disagreement to trigger extra work, abstain on severe disagreement; compare with always-revise at equal tokens.
audit_note: Self-consistency AUROC 0.823 is for Qwen2.5-3B on MATH-500 only; gap-search statements are absence claims.

claim: A linear probe on hidden activations predicts a wrong final answer from the first reasoning step (Qwen2.5-3B AUROC 0.953 vs verbalised confidence 0.674) but steering gives only +0.03 to +0.04; needs weights.
agent_test: Not testable with an API-only agent.

claim: In one university-lab task (23 students, 14 actions) CREAM gave a mean HEP of 0.062 versus 0.384 for SPAR-H (about six-fold), with only a rough indirect check against injury records; in a petrochemical control-room case a Bayesian CREAM variant gave HEPs of 0.03-0.09 vs 0.01-0.02 for basic CREAM, with no comparison to observed errors. Two case studies do not show that classical human-reliability tools generally disagree or lack validation. CREAM control-mode intervals were only seen in secondary sources.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use CREAM only as a vocabulary for cognitive-function failure modes.
audit_note: Numbers match (He 0.062 vs 0.384; Shirali 0.03-0.09 vs 0.01-0.02), but the headline generalises from one lab task and one petrochemical case to 'classical tools disagree and lack validation'; He did a rough indirect check (21 injuries, Heinrich ratio) so 'not checked' is not strictly true, and Shirali itself describes CREAM vs CREAM-BN as consistent/partly confirmed.
claim_before_audit: Classical human-reliability tools disagree and lack validation: CREAM mean HEP 0.062 vs SPAR-H 0.384 on one lab task (about six-fold), a Bayesian CREAM variant gave 0.03-0.09 vs basic 0.01-0.02, neither checked against observed errors. CREAM control-mode intervals were not opened this session. Gap search: CREAM intervals were only seen in secondary sources (strategic 0.5E-5 to 1E-2, tactical 1E-3 to 1E-1, opportunistic 1E-2 to 0.5, scrambled 0.1 to 1.0); the book was not opened.

claim: Post-error slowing in humans does not reliably produce more accurate next responses (59 ms at 200 ms interval; correlation of slowing with accuracy gain r=0.25, p=0.28); rival accounts (control, orienting, motor) remain open.
agent_test: Test whether a forced pause after a failed check changes the next attempt vs immediate retry.

claim: Trained LLM critics can help humans find code bugs (critiques preferred over human ones in 63% of natural cases) but invent bugs; a human plus critic team is better than either alone.
agent_test: Not directly applicable (needs trained critic); keep human or code as arbiter.

claim: Taxonomies of agent errors exist (module-level errors and early root-cause cascade; AgentDebug all-correct 24.3% vs 0.3%, step accuracy 45.0% vs 28.0%) and targeted feedback at the root-cause step beats unguided retry.
agent_test: Re-run from the earliest suspect step rather than regenerating everything; compare.
audit_note: Minor: 0.3% is Direct Prompting/Binary Search all-correct on AgentErrorBench; 'beats unguided retry' rests on the paper's stated comparison with scaling rollouts and unguided self-revision.

claim: Same-family reviewers: adding verifiers helps with sharply diminishing returns because errors are correlated; no study gives the joint miss rate for two reviewers from one model family.
agent_test: Run two same-model reviewers and one cross-family reviewer on seeded wrong drafts; compare joint miss rate with the product of single miss rates.

claim: Execution-grounded feedback (unit-test results, code-run errors) improves repair more than model-only critique, but an equal-token edge over resample plus vote is unproven; gains arrive in the first one to three turns.
agent_test: Equal-token test: error line from a code run plus one fix vs N resamples plus vote.
audit_note: Chen reports debugging mostly ends within 3 turns; 'unproven' equal-token edge is an absence claim supported by Olausson (1.05x/0.97x pass@20 at equal samples).

claim: Instance-specific checklists answered item by item beat holistic self-scoring and plain Self-Refine for instruction following; a fixed checklist run by code has not been tested on LLM agents.
agent_test: Fixed 5-item code-run checklist vs none on our tasks.

claim: A revise trigger pays only above about 60-70% precision on BIG-Bench Mistake; with a wrong or random location it hurts correct traces by 7-16 points. A keep-best rule is untested.
agent_test: Measure revise-trigger precision on our tasks and test keep-best-so-far.

claim: Claude-class models have no measured self-correction blind spot or false-pass rate in the sources read; Tsui tests no Claude, and Claude models show inverse scaling (accuracy down with longer reasoning) on distraction tasks.
agent_test: Measure own-draft approval of seeded wrong drafts by the agent's model vs a fresh-context reviewer.

claim: No LLM study splits errors by Reason's slip, lapse and mistake classes; MR-GSM8K names qualitative failure types only. A diary replication shows human slips are frequent and self-noticed (N=189, mean 6.4 per week).
agent_test: Tag errors in our traces as slip (copy or arithmetic) or mistake (wrong plan) and test which defence catches each.
